title: Proved polynomial-cost solution of high-dimensional nonlinear PDEs

concept.text: The innovation would be an explicit algorithm that solves a precisely defined class of nonlinear, high-dimensional parabolic partial differential equations with proved accuracy and with both runtime and memory growing polynomially in dimension d and reciprocal error 1/ε. The class would include a substantive family of nonlinear Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman (HJB) equations, which describe optimal decisions in stochastic control. The guarantee would identify the assumptions on the equations, the region where the solution is approximated, and the measure of error.

The essential advance is the connection between computational cost and guaranteed accuracy across the specified class. A successful numerical fit to selected equations does not establish that connection. The January 2026 review describes high-dimensional neural and stochastic computations, while identifying unresolved questions about approximation guarantees and coverage of the solution domain. Those findings motivate this target, but do not establish that every theorem fitting its broadly stated description is absent from the literature.

significance.text: A conventional tensor-product discretization with N degrees of freedom along each of d dimensions typically requires order N^d unknowns. This exponential growth can make storage and computation prohibitive even when each individual dimension needs only modest resolution. There is no hardware-independent dimensional cutoff: feasibility depends on accuracy, resolution, representation and available resources. A useful polynomial-cost guarantee would make certified computation possible for covered nonlinear state spaces that comparable tensor-product grids cannot represent.

The direct consequence would be certified numerical approximations within the theorem's assumptions, error norm and solution region. The review discusses HJB equations for stochastic control, Black–Scholes equations for option pricing and Fokker–Planck equations as motivating applications. Coverage of a particular HJB family would not automatically establish coverage of all these equations. Practical value would also depend on polynomial degrees and constants: polynomial asymptotic scaling alone can still entail an unaffordable computation.

Conditional downstream possibilities include more dependable evaluation of control strategies, financial models and stochastic dynamics when their equations satisfy the theorem's assumptions. These are proposed consequences, not demonstrated outcomes. A certified PDE solution would still need a justified model and an appropriate connection to the practical objective; it would not by itself implement a controller, execute a trade or establish accurate molecular electronic structure.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target is a complete error-and-cost theorem for an explicitly specified nonlinear equation class. It must bound the resources needed to reach a requested accuracy, including any sampling, approximation, optimization and input-access costs used by the algorithm. Dependence on coefficient bounds, regularity and other problem parameters must be exposed, so that exponential difficulty is not concealed in an unspecified constant or an assumed network size. Establishing which such guarantees already exist, and precisely how the proposed class would extend them, remains unresolved in the supplied evidence.

One concrete reliability barrier concerns residual-based methods evaluated along trajectories of a stochastic differential equation. The review identifies a lack of theoretical assurance that minimizing the PDE residual together with the initial-condition loss along those trajectories produces an effective approximation. Small training loss and a good benchmark result therefore do not, by themselves, supply the desired solution-error guarantee. A proof must explain how the quantities the algorithm actually controls imply accuracy for its declared output.

A separate barrier is the extent of the solution being recovered. The review highlights the difficulty of extending stochastic-trajectory methods to the whole time-space solution domain. Accuracy at selected locations, along sampled trajectories or within a sampled test region has a narrower scope than a guarantee over a declared region. The innovation must specify that scope and prove that its sampling and approximation procedure supports it, with any probabilistic confidence made explicit.

Proposed engineering requirement: the proved resource bounds must correspond to an executable implementation. If a method uses neural networks, an existence result for a compact approximation would need an accompanying way to construct or train the required network within the claimed budget. The practical challenge is to obtain useful accuracy with manageable polynomial degrees, constants and memory requirements, rather than only a favorable asymptotic classification.

current_state.text: The supplied evidence centers on the January 2026 review by Wenzhong Zhang, Zheyuan Hu, Wei Cai and George Em Karniadakis. The validated review identifies the retained full paper as version 3, dated 23 January 2026; the earlier research metadata instead described version 2 dated 22 January. The following account reflects the supplied review of that retained paper. No later literature search was documented, so this evidence does not establish the field's frontier as of 1 November 2026 or demonstrate that the target theorem remains wholly unmet.

The review lists sparse grids, low-rank tensor methods and multilevel Monte Carlo Picard iterations among approaches to mitigating dimensionality costs. These provide important alternatives to full tensor-product grids. Their inclusion does not establish a general polynomial-cost solver for the proposed nonlinear class; the applicable assumptions and guarantees must be assessed method by method.

The review's numerical comparisons report HJB and Black–Scholes benchmark results at d = 100 and d = 1000. The compared methods include a physics-informed neural-network approach labeled PINN-SDGD, Deep BSDE, DeepMartNet and Shotgun. The tables report relative L2 errors, memory use and timing, while the benchmark descriptions specify sampled test regions and Monte Carlo reference solutions. These are substantial high-dimensional demonstrations, but their measured errors and resource use do not constitute an a-priori polynomial runtime-and-memory guarantee across the proposed class.

The review also reports, through cited work, DeepMartNet applications to PDEs and stochastic optimal-control problems in up to 10,000 dimensions. The underlying cited papers were not supplied for independent inspection, so this is a report within the review. The supplied evidence does not support reassigning that dimensional claim to PINNs. Although the deep Galerkin method is discussed in the review, the reviewed benchmark tables do not establish a method-specific 1000-dimensional DGM result.

The review identifies continuing issues involving sampling, approximation guarantees and the extent of solution-domain coverage. These are specific limitations, rather than evidence that all existing high-dimensional methods lack useful guarantees. The retained PDF was reported as fully extracted without extraction issues; the abstract landing page provides only partial paper content. The supplied material also does not establish the earlier universal assertion that operator networks require precomputed solver outputs or measurements. That assertion cannot serve as a general limitation here.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed mathematical demonstration: define a substantive nonlinear parabolic PDE class containing a non-trivial HJB family across dimensions, including d ≥ 100. State the input representation, coefficient and regularity assumptions, solution notion, output representation, error norm and solution region. Prove an error bound and explicit polynomial bounds for both runtime and memory in d and 1/ε, publishing the degrees, constants and dependence on every additional problem parameter. For a randomized algorithm, specify its success probability and the cost of achieving it. These are proposed criteria, not established standards.
completion_criteria.label: Nonlinear HJB solutions have proved polynomial runtime and memory bounds

completion_criteria.text: Proposed computational demonstration: run the method at d = 1000 with its proved error bound below a tolerance fixed before the run. Document actual runtime, peak memory, the output region and the relationship between empirical error estimates and the proved guarantee. Show why a conventional tensor-product grid at comparable accuracy would exceed the stated available memory, using an explicit resolution and storage calculation. The dimension and tolerance requirements are proposed demonstrations of useful scale, not thresholds prescribed by the review.
completion_criteria.label: Proved error below preset tolerance at d=1000 with measured resources

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: release the algorithm, proof, implementation, equation definitions, parameter settings and verification procedure sufficiently completely for independent reproduction. Evaluate multiple instances spanning the declared class and relevant parameter ranges, including difficult cases near its stated boundaries. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth; the theorem would carry the class-wide guarantee within its assumptions. Neither would justify literal universality across nonlinear PDEs.
completion_criteria.label: Released methods enable independent reproduction, including difficult class-boundary cases

completion_criteria.text: A fit to one equation, a result covering only linear equations, or a guarantee conditional on an unknown or unbounded required network size would not meet this proposed target. A narrower result could still be valuable, provided its scope is explicit. Completion would require both a valid complexity theorem and evidence that its resource requirements are practical at the proposed demonstration scale.
completion_criteria.label: Valid complexity theorem and practical resource requirements at demonstration scale

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: MAT-03, “A first-principles theory of turbulent transport,” shares an interest in equations describing complex physical behavior. MAT-04 concerns certified computational cost for a specified PDE class; that capability would not itself establish a theory of turbulent transport or show that the relevant turbulence equations fall within the class.

Roster-based comparison: MAT-07, “A prescriptive mathematical theory of deep learning,” overlaps when neural networks provide the PDE approximation. A theory explaining how to choose and train networks could support MAT-04's construction and optimization guarantees. MAT-04 nevertheless has a specific numerical target and could be achieved using another algorithmic representation; it would not by itself supply a general theory of deep learning.

Roster-based comparison: MAT-08, “Polynomial-time chemical accuracy for molecular electronic structure,” also targets favorable complexity for high-dimensional scientific computation. The review names many-electron Schrödinger equations as a possible beneficiary of future advances, but does not establish their inclusion in this proposed nonlinear parabolic class. MAT-04 therefore would not imply MAT-08. The supplied evidence also does not justify identifying cancellation under antisymmetry as the exclusive electronic-structure obstruction or treating grid complexity as irrelevant there.

Roster-based comparison: MAT-05, “Research-scale machine-checked mathematical discovery,” could assist in discovering or verifying the required theorem. It concerns the mathematical discovery and verification process, whereas MAT-04 concerns the resulting PDE algorithm and its guarantees. Neither achievement establishes the other.

Roster-based comparison: MAT-01, “Practical polynomial-time algorithms for NP-complete problems,” MAT-06, “Classical polynomial-time integer factorization and discrete logarithms,” and MAT-09, “Classical polynomial-time algorithms for cryptographic lattice problems,” share the ambition of overcoming computational barriers through polynomial-time algorithms. Their discrete computational targets remain distinct from approximation of a restricted PDE class with cost measured partly by 1/ε. No reduction or implication connecting these entries is supplied.

Roster-based comparison: MAT-02, “An effective global Langlands correspondence over number fields,” concerns effective arithmetic and representation-theoretic constructions. The supplied material establishes no direct technical overlap with MAT-04 beyond their shared demand for mathematically justified, constructive procedures.

change_log.change: Preserved MAT-04's identity and theorem-backed polynomial-cost target while qualifying the assertion that the theorem is missing.
change_log.reason: The documented reliability gaps and benchmark results do not establish the absence of every qualifying theorem across the literature.

change_log.change: Separated class-wide certification, sampled benchmark accuracy and coverage of the solution domain.
change_log.reason: These are distinct scientific claims; success on sampled trajectories or test regions does not automatically establish a guarantee over a larger declared region.

change_log.change: Replaced the fixed dimensional storage cutoff with resolution- and resource-dependent tensor-grid scaling.
change_log.reason: Order N^d scaling is supported, but a universal cutoff beyond a few dozen dimensions is not.

change_log.change: Corrected benchmark attribution to PINN-SDGD, Deep BSDE, DeepMartNet and Shotgun at 100 and 1000 dimensions, and attributed the reported 10,000-dimensional applications to DeepMartNet.
change_log.reason: The reviewed tables do not establish the claimed 1000-dimensional DGM result, and the higher-dimensional statement concerns DeepMartNet rather than PINNs.

change_log.change: Qualified the 10,000-dimensional result as reported through the review and removed the universal operator-network training-data limitation.
change_log.reason: The underlying cited papers were not independently inspected, and no supplied passage establishes the asserted universal limitation.

change_log.change: Expanded the proposed completion criteria to cover error scope, confidence, parameter dependence, input costs, explicit runtime and memory bounds, reproducibility and a comparable-accuracy grid calculation.
change_log.reason: These details make the proposed demonstration assessable and prevent hidden computational costs from undermining the claimed polynomial guarantee.

change_log.change: Restricted application claims and retained MAT-08 as a distinct concept without the exclusive antisymmetry explanation.
change_log.reason: HJB coverage does not imply coverage of Fokker–Planck or electronic Schrödinger problems, and the exclusive electronic-structure obstruction was not documented.

change_log.change: Recorded the retained paper's version discrepancy and the limits of the evidence's freshness and access.
change_log.reason: The validated review identifies v3 dated 23 January 2026, whereas earlier metadata identifies v2 dated 22 January; no later search establishes the November frontier.

change_log.change: Added explicit, bounded comparisons with all other supplied roster entries.
change_log.reason: The relationships help locate MAT-04 without merging separate innovations or inventing technical implications.

unresolved_issues: The precise PDE class and its novelty relative to existing polynomial-complexity theorems remain unspecified; the supplied evidence cannot establish that the target is presently unmet.
The literature frontier as of 1 November 2026 remains unassessed because the supplied freshness search record is empty.
The discrepancy between the earlier v2 metadata and the retained v3 paper has been disclosed but its origin is unresolved.
The DeepMartNet applications up to 10,000 dimensions remain secondhand reports here; the underlying cited papers were not supplied for independent assessment.
Concrete polynomial degrees, constants, parameter dependencies, error norms and useful tolerances remain to be determined for any eventual algorithm.
The supplied roster gives titles rather than full definitions of related innovations, limiting technical comparisons, particularly with MAT-08.
